**Proposed mechanism:** JAK2 V617F mutation (rs1234567) —DISRUPTS→ JAK2 (HGNC:6076); JAK2 (HGNC:6076) —INCREASES→ JAK-STAT signaling pathway; MPL (HGNC:7508) —INCREASES→ JAK-STAT signaling pathway; SH2B3 (HGNC:10710) —DECREASES→ JAK-STAT signaling pathway; JAK-STAT signaling pathway —INCREASES→ Cytokine signaling; Cytokine signaling —LEADS_TO→ Aberrant hematopoiesis (HP:0001874); Cytokine signaling —LEADS_TO→ Myeloproliferation (HP:0001909); Cytokine signaling —LEADS_TO→ Fibrosis (HP:0002224). Gain-of-function mutations in JAK2 (e.g., V617F), MPL, or loss-of-function in SH2B3 lead to constitutive activation of the JAK-STAT signaling pathway. This dysregulates cytokine signaling, ultimately driving aberrant hematopoiesis, myeloproliferation, and fibrosis seen in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of mutations in JAK2, MPL, or SH2B3 in patients with MONDO:0014114 or primary myelofibrosis, or demonstration that these mutations do not converge on the JAK-STAT pathway. _(variant: rs1234567)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the activated JAK-STAT pathway with inhibitors could offer a shared therapeutic strategy for both MONDO:0014114 and primary myelofibrosis.
